title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1969-12-19
lineage: DAT (Sony PCM-R500) > Tascam DA-3000 > Samplitude Pro X6 Suite > FLAC

ai_review.summary: Great‑sound soundboard capture of a fun acoustic opener and the debut of Mason’s Children.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers clear, well‑balanced audio—especially the acoustic set that opens the show—and even includes an audience patch for Casey Jones that preserves the entire performance. Musically the concert is memorable: Phil was late, so Bob and Jerry led a rare four‑song acoustic set of first‑time‑played tunes and the band debuted “Mason’s Children.” Overall it’s a fun, historically interesting show with solid sound.

ai_rating.rationale: Review is enthusiastic (4★) and highlights both good sound quality and unique musical moments; limited to a single review, so confidence is medium.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, crisp audio throughout; acoustic set sounds especially clean. An audience‑source patch is used for Casey Jones, but overall the mix remains balanced and listenable.

standout_songs: I've Been All Around This World
show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic opener by Bob & Jerry due to Phil’s late arrival, followed by the full band set; the unusual start and debut of Mason's Children give the show a unique flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Leads acoustic opening with solid guitar work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Late to the show, missing the acoustic opener.
band_member_comments.Bob: Shares acoustic duties on the early set, delivering strong rhythm and vocals.
